description: Figure 6 is a three-panel composite of SEM images of tensile fracture surfaces of three heat-treated Fe–20Mn–9Al-1.5C–2Ni–3Cr low-density steels: (a) S1000, (b) S1050 and (c) MHT. Each panel is a high-magnification fracture-surface micrograph carrying a white "Dimple" annotation with white arrows marking individual dimples and a 10 µm scale bar at the lower right. In the lower-left corner of every panel a yellow-bordered low-magnification inset (the caption calls these reduction maps with yellow border) shows the whole fractured specimen with a 0.5 mm scale bar. (a) shows dimples of strongly non-uniform size, with a few large deep dimples several micrometres across enclosed by walls of finer dimples; (b) shows a finer, denser dimple network together with a cluster of deeper round holes pointed to by arrows; (c) shows a dimple network that appears shallower, more equiaxed and less developed. The insets show rectangular specimens with a rough central fracture region and shear-lip-like bands along the edges. Taken together the panels demonstrate that all three steels failed by ductile dimple rupture, while dimple size, depth and uniformity differ between S1000, S1050 and MHT. No numeric dimple dimensions are printed on any panel.

observations.observation: Each of the three panels is a secondary-electron SEM image of a tensile fracture surface bearing the white annotation "Dimple" and white arrows pointing at individual dimples.
Every panel contains two scale references: a 10 µm scale bar at the lower right of the main micrograph and a yellow-bordered low-magnification inset with a 0.5 mm scale bar at the lower left.
In (a) the dimples are clearly non-uniform in size, with a small number of large deep dimples roughly several micrometres across surrounded by walls of finer dimples.
Panel (b) shows a finer and denser dimple network than (a), together with a cluster of deeper round holes marked by arrows in the upper-right region.
Panel (c) (MHT) shows a dimple network that appears shallower, more equiaxed and less developed than the dimples in (a) and (b), separated by prominent ridge walls.
The low-magnification insets of all three panels show a rectangular specimen cross-section with a rough central fracture region and shear-lip-like bands along the edges.
No numeric dimple size, area fraction or axis values are printed on any panel; only the 10 µm and 0.5 mm scale bars provide dimensional reference.
The caption assigns the panels as (a) S1000, (b) S1050 and (c) MHT, and describes the insets as low-magnification reduction maps with yellow border.
The citing text states that Fig. 6 shows SEM tensile fracture images of the three experimental steels and that all steels show dimples, but the dimples are not uniform in size.
The citing text asserts that Cr7C3 on the grain boundaries of S1000 and B2 in the grains of S1050 and MHT do not significantly decrease the ductility of the steels.

The citing text states that underdeveloped dimples are present in MHT and its plasticity is also slightly reduced; the image itself shows only a shallower dimple network and does not quantify plasticity.
